sections.title: Prologue: The Book's Claims and the Coded Message
sections.summary: The prologue introduces this book as a demonstration, produced with the aid of a Hewlett-Packard computer, of physical and verifiable proof for the existence of God, a message from God to the reader, and the exact year the world will end. It states that God's coded message arrived to the world through a man from Arabia named Muhammad, released over 23 years in Arabic, and that all evidence in the book is simplified into verse-by-verse alphabet-letter counts so any reader can randomly spot-check the data. sections.title: Why the Number Nineteen: Chapter 74 and the Word 'Wahid'
sections.summary: This section argues that the fourth revelation, verses 1 through 30 of chapter 74 ('The Hidden Secret'), introduced the number 19 itself, declaring that anyone who calls the Quran man-made will be proven wrong by that number, and lists five stated purposes of the code: to stump disbelievers, reassure Jews and Christians, strengthen believers' faith, remove doubt, and expose hypocrites. sections.title: Epilogue: Calculating the Year the World Will End
sections.summary: The epilogue argues that the 14 sets of Quranic initials, described as the 'seven pairs' mentioned in chapter 15 verse 87, represent the length of Muhammad's prophetic interim in years when their numerical letter-values are summed, yielding 1,789 lunar years.
